4.13 If, as a result of questioning the person, or of other circumstances which come
to the attention of the constable, a constable’s re asonable grounds for suspicion are
confirmed, or if reasonable grounds for suspicion e merge during an encounter, the
constable may detain the person to search them. Rea sonable grounds for suspicion
however cannot be provided retrospectively by such questioning during a person’s
detention, or by refusal to answer any questions asked.
